text.title: Python FastAPI — Procedure
text.summary: Eight-step procedure for applying python-fastapi, from dependency bootstrap to the CI gate.

section.title: Step 0: Bootstrap the async stack
section.p: Input: Python 3.11+, a dependency manager

Action: Install `fastapi[standard] pydantic-settings sqlalchemy[asyncio] asyncpg alembic uvicorn`. Lay out `app/` as main.py + config.py + dependencies.py + routers/ + schemas/ + services/ + models/ + db/.
Output: pyproject.toml + lockfile + the package skeleton.
Decision gate: a non-async database driver aborts this methodology — every rule below assumes an AsyncSession.

section.title: Step 0b: Lifespan and dependency aliases
section.p: Input: templates/main.py + templates/dependencies.py
Action: Create the app with an `@asynccontextmanager` lifespan opening and disposing the engine; declare `DBSession` and `CurrentUser` Annotated aliases; gate docs_url on settings.debug.
Output: app/main.py + app/dependencies.py.
Decision gate: any surviving `@app.on_event` blocks (rule r7-lifespan-not-on-event).

section.title: Step 1: Define Pydantic schemas
section.p: Input: Endpoint spec
Action: For each entity author the quartet in `app/schemas/<entity>.py` — Base (shared), Create (input), Update (all optional), Response (output, `ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)`).
Output: Typed boundaries; one schemas module per entity.
Decision gate: reject a single model serving several roles (rule r8-schema-quartet).

section.title: Step 2: Write service function
section.p: Input: Schemas exist

Action: Author `app/services/<entity>.py` — `async def`, takes an AsyncSession plus typed values, returns an ORM instance or None. Use `await db.flush(); await db.refresh(obj)` for generated ids; never commit inside a service.
Output: Service unit-testable without HTTP.
Decision gate: routers import services, never models directly (rules r10-services-return-orm, r11-flush-refresh-not-commit).

section.title: Step 3: Wire route
section.p: Input: Service exists
Action: Add APIRouter route that validates, calls service, returns Out.
Output: Thin route.

section.title: Step 4: Register dependencies
section.p: Input: Route wired
Action: Add Depends(get_session) and any auth/permission deps.
Output: DI complete.

section.title: Step 5: Snapshot openapi
section.p: Input: App boots
Action: Generate openapi.json; commit to repo; add CI diff job.
Output: Drift guard.

section.title: Step 6: Audit for blocking calls
section.p: Input: The routes and services just written

Action: Grep the async modules for `requests.`, sync `Session`, `open(` on a hot path and `time.sleep`. Replace with `httpx.AsyncClient`, `AsyncSession`, or `run_in_threadpool` where the library has no async form.
Output: No blocking call reachable from a coroutine.
Decision gate: one blocking call is enough to erase the benefit of the whole async stack (rule r12-no-sync-io-in-async-route).

section.title: Step 7: Wire the CI gate
section.p: Input: pre-commit + CI
Action: Run ruff, mypy --strict, pytest, the openapi diff, and scripts/validate-python-fastapi.py on every PR.
Output: Updated CI workflow.
Decision gate: block merge on any gate failure.
